title: Docs Media Report Delivery
summary: DMR-1 through DMR-3 shipped and closed after manual acceptance and ownership transfer
content_html:
Docs Media Report Delivery

Status And Purpose

This delivery is complete and closed. The exact rows, local route, report registration and Dotlineform host, focused three-column module, manual acceptance, focused closeout evidence, and durable ownership transfer are complete. The retained delivery records bounded implementation evidence; no second media report or management action started at closeout.

Complete Outcome

One manage-only Docs Media report document in the Dotlineform scope uses the Project State list format to show one row per distinct exact ready-media or registered build-source file returned by the selected configured parent scope's live storage listing. Its only columns are sortable Type, File name, and Documents. Type displays the configured ready-media or build-source type; File name displays the relative identity and reveals its exact role-specific external-workspace target in Finder. Each Documents cell contains exact /docs/ links directly associated with that identity and is blank when the file is unreferenced. Its toolbar contains a scope selector, refresh pill, and search across file names and document titles. Referenced identities absent from the live listing do not appear; a separate future Media Broken Links report will own those.

DMR-1 — Exact Media Rows

  • [x] Produce one row for each distinct {scope, media_type, identity} returned by the live listing of configured ready-media and build-source locations.
  • [x] Collect distinct exact document title and Manage URL entries directly associated with each row, deduplicating repeated occurrences only within the same document and never inferring identity from title, route, selected row, report context, or a same-basename derived output.
  • [x] Return separate exact media_type and relative identity values plus the confined role-specific Projects-relative local target for each listed file; build-source/mermaid/<identity> returns Type mermaid.
  • [x] Include existing unreferenced ready-media and build-source files with no document entries; do not materialize rows from referenced identities absent from the live listing.
  • [x] Keep absolute paths, credentials, raw provider exceptions, retained-original evidence, and filesystem authority server-side.

Stop after this checkpoint for review before the report UI.

DMR-1 Review Evidence

  • Reused docs_media_inventory.py for provider-neutral ready-media/build-source listing and its existing canonical reference parser, accepting the complete collected parent/sub-scope reference set so the report does not add or rerun a second scanner.
  • Added the focused docs_media_report_v1 read model in docs_media_report.py; it returns only scope, media_type, identity, encoded Projects-relative local_target, and exact ordered document target, title, and Manage href entries.
  • Focused fixture evidence covers nested identities, same-document deduplication, several exact parent/sub-scope documents for one file, repeated titles, unreferenced ready-media and build-source rows, Mermaid source/output separation, missing-reference omission, and private-field/path exclusion.
  • Verification on 2026-08-12: the new report and unchanged inventory suites passed 7 tests; changed Python syntax and lint passed; git diff --check passed. A read-only run against the configured Dotlineform workspace returned 344 live files/img rows, all currently referenced.

DMR-2 — Project State-Format List

  • [x] Register one local Docs Media report and one report-backed host document in the Dotlineform scope.
  • [x] Render the Project State list-backed table with only sortable Type, File name, and Documents columns, defaulting to Type then File name ascending and using the exact complementary fields as deterministic tie-breakers.
  • [x] Add a toolbar containing only a configured-scope selector defaulting to Dotlineform, a refresh pill, and the Project State-style search field with clear control; persist the scope as report_scope.
  • [x] Make refresh rerun the selected scope's live ready-media and build-source listing plus document join while preserving and reapplying current search and sort state.
  • [x] Filter loaded rows by case-insensitive substring match against the displayed File name or any document title, excluding Type from search and using a contained no-match state distinct from an empty scope.
  • [x] Render Type as plain configured-id text; reveal each live-listed ready-media or build-source file from its File name link through the current local-target action; stack exact direct document links and leave an unreferenced file's Documents cell blank.
  • [x] Keep the report module and local read seam absent from public routes.

DMR-2 Review Evidence

  • Registered docs_media as a local-only report, added the exact-scope POST /docs/media-report response, and reused the current report service and confined local-target action without adding a public route or a second activation path.
  • Added one focused list module with exactly Type, File name, and Documents; the configured-scope selector, refresh pill, identity/document-title search, clear control, persistent scope and sort state, deterministic three-column sorting, stacked exact document targets, blank document cells, and distinct scope-empty, search-empty, unavailable, and failure states remain within that module.
  • Created the report-backed Docs Media host through the current Docs management create, source-rebuild, and metadata seams. Its generated descriptor is local docs_media with no forced scope, so the module defaults to Dotlineform and retains scope selection.
  • Focused verification on 2026-08-12: the report, unchanged inventory, route, report-source, contract, and public-boundary suites passed 86 tests; the browser module smoke passed; changed Python and JavaScript lint, docs/search builds, generated-projection checks, and git diff --check passed. A direct live local response for Dotlineform returned schema docs_media_report_v1 with 344 rows: 328 img and 16 files.

DMR-3 — Verify And Transfer Ownership

  • [x] Manually review representative Dotlineform density, all configured media types, nested relative identities, several documents for one file, repeated document titles, blank unreferenced cells, long file names, scope changes, refresh, file-name and document-title searches, all three sorts, empty and no-match results, exact document navigation, Finder reveal, and omission of missing referenced identities.
  • [x] Run only the focused read-model, direct response, registration/module, public-isolation, changed-source lint, docs-build, and git diff --check evidence warranted by the implemented seams.
  • [x] Transfer the stable report contract to Reports and Media And Asset Handling, present the closeout list, and stop before any second media report or management action.

DMR-3 Closeout Record

  • The user completed manual review and approved closeout on 2026-08-12. The DMR-3 representative presentation, interaction, navigation, Finder reveal, and omission checklist is accepted.
  • The closeout rerun passed 86 focused report, inventory, route, report-source, contract, and public-boundary tests plus the focused browser module smoke. The live Dotlineform response remained docs_media_report_v1 with 344 rows: 328 img and 16 files. Changed Python and JavaScript lint, Python syntax, report-registry JSON validation, targeted Studio docs/search consistency with zero warnings, and git diff --check also passed.
  • Reports now owns the current local report registration, route, presentation, controls, and public-exclusion summary. Media And Asset Handling owns the live-file row, exact-reference, confined-target, storage, and non-goals contract.
  • The completed feature parent, concept, and this delivery remain as retained Roadmap history. Closeout does not retire them and does not authorize Media Broken Links, media mutation, source repair, publication changes, or another media-management slice.

Likely Owners To Inspect

This is a broad owner map, not a fixed file or test plan:

boundary likely owner
Live ready-media and build-source objects, exact document references, and unreferenced files existing provider-independent media inventory service
Exact document link existing scope/sub-scope document target and Manage URL owners
Finder activation existing confined local-target service and report client
Local response existing Docs management read service and route registration
UI host report metadata, one Dotlineform report document, and one focused Manage report module
Presentation, controls, search, and sorting existing Project State list/table, toolbar, refresh, search, empty-state, query-state, and sortable-header patterns

Verification Stance

Use the smallest checks that protect the actual seams:

  • focused pure/service cases for live ready-media and build-source row grouping, Mermaid type/target projection, parent and sub-scope attribution, same-document deduplication, exact document URLs, blank unreferenced rows, no inferred source/output relationship, and omission of missing referenced identities;
  • one direct read-contract test when the response crosses the local HTTP seam;
  • the smallest existing report module/loader check for scope selection, refresh, two-field search, sorting, stacked links, blank cells, empty states, and registration; and
  • manual UI review for density, refresh, search, sorting, scope switching, navigation, Finder activation, and general workflow feel.

Do not add a broad smoke profile, duplicate public-isolation suites, or permanent browser choreography tests. Reuse an existing durable boundary check when one already proves that Manage-only report modules and local APIs stay out of public entrypoints.

Not In Scope

  • Aggregate counts, byte totals, additional filters, detail views, grouping controls, copy controls, or retained-original evidence.
  • Missing-reference rows, broken-link diagnosis, or delivery of the separate future Media Broken Links report.
  • Inferred build-source-to-output relationships or copying an output file's document references onto its build-source row.
  • Media mutation, source association, source repair, replacement, relinking, deletion, publication, provider movement, or automatic orphan cleanup.
  • Hashing, byte comparison, background jobs, caches, thumbnails, OCR, content indexing, or archive expansion.
  • A registry, semantic media target, nested managed identity, multiple active destinations, or Media Publication Check behavior.
  • Rollback copies, rollback actions, automatic retry, recovery orchestration, or transaction frameworks.
  • A generic report plugin, schema-driven dashboard, second reference scanner, or parallel local-file activation path.

Completion Evidence

  • Every ready-media and registered build-source file returned by the live listing produces one exact grouped row; absent referenced identities do not.
  • Existing ready-media and build-source files reveal the selected object in Finder; unreferenced files remain visible with a blank Documents cell.
  • Every referencing document link preserves exact parent and sub-scope identity, including repeated titles.
  • The report opens in Dotlineform with Dotlineform selected, changes scope through the selector, refreshes the live listing, searches file names and document titles, and sorts all three columns deterministically.
  • The local read seam and report module remain absent from public entrypoints through the smallest existing or focused boundary evidence.
  • Reports and Media And Asset Handling receive only the stable shipped contract at closeout.

DMR-1 through DMR-3 completed and closed on 2026-08-12. The shipped contract now lives with Reports and Media And Asset Handling; later media work requires a separate delivery.
